text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The management board of private bank Bankcoop SA have approved a new management formula. The new Bankcoop's chairman will be Alexandru Ghiba, who was first vice-president of the state-run commercial bank Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The government is expected to approve the draft 1997 state buget on Tuesday.
ADEVARUL

- Romanian officials hope the first tranche of an International Monetary Fund loan will help the local leu currency to stabilise in the second half of the year, the deputy speaker of the Senate said on Monday.
- Many small enterprises post huge losses due to the depreciation of the leu over the past three months, the newspaper said.
General:
All the newspapers report President Emil Constantinescu's official visit to the Czech Republic.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Chris Donnelly, special adviser to NATO's secretary-general for central and eastern Europe said Romania had made "spectacular progress" in its bid to join the NATO in the first wave.
- Some 90 percent of Romania's drug addicts take heroine, the newspaper says in a report.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper comments on Russia's Duma's decision not to return Romania's treasury taken by the former Soviet Union.
- Too many people die in car accidents, says Colonel Dumitru Ciubotea, head of the Romanian traffic police in an interview. In the first two months of this year 290 people died, he says.
ADEVARUL
- This century's last solar eclipse, due in 1999, will be best seen in Bucharest, the only place in the world where people will be able to observe the phenomenon for more than two minutes.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
